intent: Close the server-side authority breach in issue #1508 by making the leg-one Helm reject approval.resolve without working-memory, SessionStore, RuntimeStateStore, permission-resolution, or permission-outcome effects, while preserving read-only approval history and inbound permission projections.

negative_controls.name: approval-working-memory-effect-is-detected

commit.message: fix(helm): enforce the read-only approval boundary

interface_mismatches: The binding leg-one spec admits a read-only instrument, but current action.run handling treats approval.resolve as a locally effectful command and writes both runtime and session stores.

The TypeScript shell still advertises approve, deny, and dismiss controls. This packet makes those calls harmless at the authority boundary; a separate two-layer UI packet removes the misleading affordance.
Inbound permission decisions, outcomes, resolutions, and history are observations owned by upstream runtime/governance paths and must remain renderable after local mutation is denied.
honest_blockers: This packet closes only the bridge-side mutation seam. The current TypeScript approval affordance remains visible until a separately governed Terminal Guardian slice removes or disables it.
The protected live Helm session is not restarted or modified by this packet, so its running old bridge remains unchanged until a later verified cutover.
Zero local writes do not prove owner projections, seven-seat liveness, terminal performance, or production readiness.
session_entry.rollback: Revert the packet commit to restore the previous approval.resolve behavior in source. No runtime store migration or data deletion is part of this change; any pre-existing approval rows remain untouched.
